text:
maya li: thinking aloud — we need a simpler surface for ops + customers to pick quant profiles without leaking complexity. right now profiles are inscrutable lists of layer rules.
prateek rao: agreed. customers keep asking for a single knob like `latency vs quality` instead of per-layer maps.
alex g: +1. but we also need a clear runtime contract for fallbacks. if a profile triggers an error we should define deterministic behavior.
jen h: proposal: expose two things — a compact "quality tier" (high/medium/eco) and an escape hatch header for advanced profiles. keep the advanced DSL but hide it behind UI/SDK.
samir: love that. runtime checklist idea:
- client sends quality tier header: `X-Redwood-Precision-Tier: eco|balanced|high`
- server maps tier -> quant profile (internal)
- runtime returns `precision:path` telemetry when fallback occurs
- automatic fallback order: fp8 -> int8 -> int4 -> fp16
maya li: code sketch for header handling in SDK:
```
// pseudo
headers["X-Redwood-Precision-Tier"] = "eco"
// SDK also supports: headers["X-Redwood-Precision-Profile"] = "cust:profile-id"
```
prateek rao: on the fallback order — do we always allow int4 as last resort? some models catastrophically degrade with 4-bit.
alex g: we should gate int4 behind a canary + quality escrow. i.e. only enable int4 if model's regression < threshold on daily validation set.
jen h: telemetry to make actionable: include `degradation_score` in logs with histogram buckets, and surface per-endpoint alerts when it spikes.
samir: ops ergonomics: UI should let support override a customer's tier per-endpoint and roll back. also add a `preview` API that simulates inference under a profile for developer testing.
maya li: suggestion for preview API shape:
```
POST /v1/preview-precision
body: { model: "redwood-13b", prompt: "...", profile: "eco" }
response: { tokens: [...], degradation_score: 0.12, diffs: [ { span: "1-20", metric: "f1", delta: -0.03 } ] }
```
prateek rao: important: preview must be cheap. run on a small sample and return aggregated deltas, not full output unless requested.
alex g: runtime surface decision: we return a hint header when we actually used a lower-precision path, e.g. `X-Redwood-Precision-Used: int8` so customers can correlate.
jen h: ops-bot idea — add an automated triage that fires when degradation_score > 0.2 and routes to ML oncall with attached canary snapshots.
ops-bot: automated-detection: detected degradation spike on endpoint "search-embeddings-prod". sample_id=98345. opened ticket RW-8421 :rotating_light:
samir: what about per-customer SLAs? customers with strict quality should be able to pin `precision:fp16` or `precision:fp32` to avoid falls.
maya li: yep. policy matrix: free tiers get eco (aggressive), paid can pick balanced/high, enterprise can pin fixed precision.
prateek rao: one more edge: weight-only vs activation quant differences. profiles should distinguish "weight-only" quant (safer) vs full-graph quant. map tier -> conservative weight-only by default.
alex g: ops question — how do we version profiles? we need immutable profile ids and rollout metadata (who rolled, when, canary fraction).
jen h: rollout plan:
- create profile v1 as `eco-v1` with immutable id
- canary at 1% on low-traffic endpoints for 48h
- monitor degradation_score + latency + cost
- promote to 10% then 50% then 100% with automated rollback on regressions
maya li: for storage: profiles live in config service, pinned by endpoint. include `compatibility` field listing supported model families.
samir: UX: in console show a small snippet: "Predicted cost savings: 24% | Expected median latency: -20ms | Risk: medium (0.08 deg)" and a single-click enable.
prateek rao: operational telemetry to collect: per-request `profile_id`, `precision_used`, `degradation_score`, `latency_p50/p95`, `cost_delta_estimate`.
alex g: ops-telemetry payload example (json):
```
{
  "profile_id": "eco-v1",
  "precision_used": "int8",
  "degradation_score": 0.07,
  "latency_p95": 210
}
```
jen h: final ask: we should avoid exposing raw bitwidths in defaults. naming tiers by outcomes (eco/balanced/high) keeps customers focused on tradeoffs not bits.
maya li: agreed. action items:
- prateek: spec preview API + sampling budget (due EOW)
- alex: add header hints + telemetry fields to runtime contract (PR)
- jen: console mockups for single-click enable and rollback
- samir: ops playbook for canary + automated triage
- maya: write short RFC backing the ergonomics rationale
prateek rao: noted. starting a doc in google drive, will drop link soon.
maya li: thanks everyone :pray:
